newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's Mobutu wants envoy to stand trial in France.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu wants envoy to stand trial in France.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko will allow a Zairean envoy who accidentally ran over two schoolboys in Menton, southern France, to stand trial as Paris has demanded, an aide said on Tuesday.

"The president of the Republic has assured the mayor of Menton that he will make sure that the Zairean government grants the request for the lifting of Ambassador Ramazani Baya's diplomatic immunity," Mobutu aide Atumba Ngbanda told reporters.

Ngbanda said Baya had informed Mobutu that he would ask the Zairean government to lift his immunity so that he could stand trial in connection with the deaths of the boys, who were run over by Baya's car in the Riviera resort on November 23.

The diplomat's status had become a sticking point in ties between Kinshasa and Paris after the French Foreign Ministry demanded that Baya be withdrawn and urged that he be brought to justice in France.

Police say the ambassador was driving at 100 kph (62 mph) in a 45-kph (30-mph) zone when his car hit the two boys on a pedestrian crossing. Raphael Lenoir, 13, was killedinstantly. Ronald Lehartel, 12, died on Saturday after a prolonged coma.

The incident has embarrassed France as well as Zaire by putting the focus on the presence of Mobutu, a pariah banned from much of Europe and the United States, in his palatial Riviera mansion during a crisis over hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire.
